importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — a security cabin, 1BHK residential unit, bunkhouse, and portable shop are all visually distinct products within this MCAT. Buyers use the image to identify the product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.
Size (L×W) and room configuration are non-negotiable shortlisting criteria — a 10×10 ft plain cabin and a 20×40 ft 1BHK are not substitutable. Buyers cannot evaluate a listing without these specs.

This is a significant capital purchase and Indian B2B buyers compare prices aggressively across sellers. Price changes substantially with size and room configuration, so buyers discover and compare across spec tiers — making price a primary decision lever after size and configuration match.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom-dimension orders are quoted per sq ft; standard catalogue sizes (10ft–40ft) are quoted per piece. Both units appear in the market — unit must be shown alongside price to prevent comparison errors.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece vs per sq ft is a documented market ambiguity for this MCAT. Price cannot be meaningfully compared across listings without knowing the unit, particularly when buyers receive both catalogue and custom quotes simultaneously.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — the market is dominated by unorganised MSME fabricators and taxonomy siblings are material/type-based, not brand-based.
importance_ranking.reason: For bulk or institutional orders (labour colonies, government procurement), seller installation capability, AMC, and track record are evaluated during vendor selection. For smaller orders, company is less decisive than spec and price.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — a 6×4 ft security cabin and a 40×10 ft residential unit are non-interchangeable and carry a massive price delta; no buyer can substitute one size for another.

Defines the quality and cost tier within a given size — MS Sheet (basic) vs PUF Panel (insulated premium) vs ACP Panel (premium finish) carry significant price deltas and buyers with thermal comfort or finish requirements cannot accept lower-grade panels.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Whether a unit is a plain cabin, single room with toilet, or 1BHK with kitchen is a primary buyer requirement that determines product type and price tier — absent from the seller spec list entirely.

Panel thickness (e.g., 50mm, 75mm, 100mm) determines thermal performance and structural rigidity — a standard differentiator in the Indian prefab market that buyers use to compare insulation quality across sellers.

Floor-to-ceiling height is a standard structural dimension for portable structures that affects usability and ventilation — buyers and sellers both need this to confirm the unit meets site requirements.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines what the buyer fundamentally needs — a plain cabin vs a 1BHK with bathroom and kitchen are different products at very different price points, and sellers must know this to determine fit and quote accurately.
Primary dimensional spec that drives floor area and price — Length spans 10–40 ft with major price implications, giving sellers the most discriminating single dimension to assess fit and quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires basic MS sheet panels, PUF-insulated panels, or ACP finish panels — this materially changes the price and determines whether the seller can supply the right product.
